newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt says CPI rise due to seasonal factors.
newsitem.headline: French govt says CPI rise due to seasonal factors.

text.p: The French finance ministry said on Friday the 0.4 percent rise in consumer prices in September was due mostly to seasonal factors.

"Like the declines in previous months, but in the opposite direction, the significant rise in the price index reported in September can be explained principally by seasonal factors and the price of oil," the ministry said in a statement.
National statistics institute INSEE reported earlier that consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in September, giving a year-on-year rise of 1.6 percent.
In August, consumer prices in France fell 0.3 percent following drops of 0.2 percent in July and 0.1 percent in June.
The August year-on-year inflation rate was 1.6 percent.
The finance ministry said a seasonal increase in fresh produce prices and the end of summer clothing sales were important factors behind the rise.
It said the stability of the year-on-year rate of inflation showed prices had returned to their long term trend levels after absorbing a rise in value added tax (VAT) in August 1995.

"Beyond monthly fluctuations, it is worth underlining that the year-on-year rise of the price index is unchanged at 1.6 percent, which confirms a return to the trend which prevailed before the increase in the normal VAT rate," the ministry's statement said.
It added that the year-on-year rate was consistent with government projections of a year-on-year rate of inflation of 1.5 percent at the end of the year.
